newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude stays flat, Dated trades in range.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude stays flat, Dated trades in range.

text.p: North Sea crudes showed few signs of recovering from recent depressed levels on Wednesday amid ample April supply and muted U.S. demand, traders said.
A minimum Brent cargo, loading April 8-10, traded at May Brent -97 cents a barrel, three cents weaker than a deal on Tuesday but only a cent off Monday's level.
Traders said sentiment remained soft after the release of industry data showing U.S. crude stocks rose by over six million barrels last week.
May Brent shed eight cents to $19.03 a barrel by 1211 GMT and April 7-11 CFDs lost about five cents.
Norwegian Ekofisk fetched Dated Brent -3 cents, in line with trade on Tuesday and Statfjord loading April 9-11 fetched a steady Dated Brent +7 cents.
Traders said the cancellation of a fifth Forties cargo from the April programme due to underperformance at the Scott field was doing little to erase prompt oversupply.
"What we need is another 10 to get back to parity," said a trader.
Two Brents were nominated April 17-19 loading dates on Wednesday but traders said the fate of the grade was still in the hands of BP who holds about 10 unsold cargoes.
On the West African market, a cargo of Forcados changed hands earlier this week at Dated Brent -20 cents, towards the weaker end of current price assessments.
An April 22-23 cargo of Bonny Light was offered at Dated +25 cents, while a Qua Iboe was offered at Dated +20 cents.
"It's a very thin market with little interest at present," a trader said.

Traders said Shell had restored operations at all the flow stations west of the Niger Delta disrupted by political unrest last week. All production in the Nembe area of the eastern division had also been restored.
